thread_text:
Priya Nair: Heads-up — SRE Pager alerted on SLO burn for /v1/generate tokens. 10m burn spiked to ~3x and paged primary oncall. I'm putting initial notes here while I triage.
SRE Pager: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO_BURN_TOKEN_GEN (service: inference/runtime) — 10m burn 3.0x, 1h burn 1.4x. Paging primary oncall. Incident ID INC-2025-108.
OpsBot: Automated runbook invoked: runbook/slo-burn -> collecting span traces and recent deploys.
Maya Patel: Oncall here, joining. Any obvious deploys in last 30m?
Priya Nair: No user-facing deploys. A small infra config rolling update landed ~45m ago to batcher autoscaler (non-customer-facing) — checking if correlation.
Luke Chen: I see elevated queue wait times on a subset of pods in eu-west-1. Logs show intermittent OOMs on model shard workers, followed by pod restarts. Might explain short-term burn.
Zara Gomez: Can you paste the alert query? I'm curious what windows we page for.
Priya Nair: Query pasted below for context:
```
sum(rate(slo_burn_tokens_total{service="inference/runtime"}[10m]))
/
sum(slo_budget_tokens_total{service="inference/runtime"})
```
Paging rule is 10m window > 2.0x or 1h window > 1.5x.
Maya Patel: Ok — looks like the 10m path is noisy because restarts spike short-window burn. We should avoid paging on single 10m blips unless sustained or accompanied by customer impact signals.
Priya Nair: Agree. Customers? Any CS hits or support tickets?
Zara Gomez: Searching support — two customers reported slow responses in the last 20m (non-blocking). No major errors, just latency.
SRE Pager: Note: auto-escalation to paging occurs immediately for 10m threshold.
Luke Chen: Mitigation: I've cordoned the affected node group and forced pods to restart on healthy hosts. Also kicked a temporary scale-up of model workers in eu-west-1. Monitoring shows queue depth decreasing.
Maya Patel: Nice. Can we change the paging to require either 10m>3x OR sustained 3x over 15m for a page? That would cut noise but still page on real outages.
Priya Nair: Proposal: adjust paging criteria to: (10m > 3.0) OR (15m > 2.0) OR (60m > 1.5). Also add a secondary check that customer-facing error rate increase >0.5% to page regardless. Thoughts?
Zara Gomez: I like adding a customer-facing signal. Otherwise infra flapping triggers pages w/o tangible impact.
Luke Chen: Implementation note — the alert backend supports multi-window thresholds but we need to ensure we don't lose SLIs in the console. I'll open a PR against alerting-config and add a guard in the escalation policy.
Maya Patel: Action items: Luke to open PR and patch escalation; Priya to update runbook section on multi-window handling; Zara to create a short dashboard tile for customer-facing impact signals (error-rate & support inbound). I'll take post-incident coordination and run a quick retro after stability confirmed.
Priya Nair: Putting estimated timeline: PR in next 30m, deploy change after 2pm UTC approval. For now, I disabled auto-paging for the 10m threshold (temporary) to prevent additional noise while we stabilize.
OpsBot: Config change recorded: alerting/auto-paging/disable_temp (user=Priya Nair, reason=incident noise mitigation).
Luke Chen: PR: https://git.internal/r/alerting/+/2547 — changes multiwindow rules + escalation policy. Ready for review.
Zara Gomez: Dashboard draft: https://dashboards/redwood/slo-burn-incident-180555 — added tokens burn, queue depth, customer error-rate panel.
Maya Patel: :thumbsup: Good. Once queue depth is stable and pod OOMs stop for 30m, we'll re-enable normal paging thresholds.
Priya Nair: Current status: queue depth trending down, 10m burn back to 1.1x. Keeping watch.
SRE Pager: Incident INC-2025-108 moved to status: monitoring.
Maya Patel: Post-incident to-dos: (1) follow-up with infra team on autoscaler root cause, (2) formalize multi-window paging policy in runbooks, (3) add a suppressed-incidents tag for transient infra flaps in alerts so we can report them separately. I'll volunteer to write the policy doc.
Priya Nair: I'll take infra follow-up and include logs & OOM traces in the incident folder.
Zara Gomez: I'll run a short eval on whether quantization fallback increased latency on shard restarts (just in case).
Luke Chen: Thanks everyone — I'll merge PR after one LGTM and push live.
Maya Patel: Closing note: thanks to quick mitigation — customer impact limited. We'll plan a retro tomorrow. :coffee:
